title: Jensen Huang
paragraphs: Jen-Hsun "Jensen" Huang (born February 17, 1963) is a Taiwanese and American electrical engineer and business executive who is the co-founder, president, and chief executive officer (CEO) of Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies. As of November 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth at US$143.4 billion, making him the 13th-wealthiest person in the world.

Born in Taipei, Huang spent his childhood in Taiwan and Thailand before immigrating to the United States. After earning a master's degree from Stanford University, he launched Nvidia alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem from a Denny's restaurant in San Jose, California, in 1993. Huang led the company out of near-bankruptcy during the 1990s and oversaw its expansion from graphics processing unit (GPU) development into high-performance computing and artificial intelligence (AI).

Under Huang's leadership, Nvidia experienced massive growth during the AI boom, becoming the first company to reach a market capitalization of more than $5 trillion in 2025. He briefly resigned from his positions at Nvidia in 2026 after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of Chinese espionage, but was reinstated soon after.

In 2021 and 2024, Time magazine included Huang in its list of the most influential people, and later named him as one of the "Architects of AI" for its 2025 Person of the Year. He was also awarded the IEEE Medal of Honor and the National Medal of Science in 2026 for his contributions to machine learning and computational science.
